```{r}
#| include: false
library(tibble)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
options(scipen = 999)

usd <- function(x) paste0("$", format(round(x), big.mark = ","))

# Dark technology theme for all charts
accent <- "#0066FF"   # electric blue (recommended option / highlights)
warm   <- "#FF7A45"   # orange (second series)
muted  <- "#94A3B8"   # slate gray (third series)
panel  <- "#FFFFFF"
gridln <- "#E2E8F0"

theme_tech <- function(base_size = 14) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.background   = element_rect(fill = panel, color = NA),
      panel.background  = element_rect(fill = panel, color = NA),
      panel.grid.major  = element_line(color = gridln),
      panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
      text              = element_text(color = "#334155"),
      axis.text         = element_text(color = "#64748B"),
      plot.title        = element_text(color = "#0B1F3A", face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle     = element_text(color = "#64748B"),
      legend.background = element_rect(fill = panel, color = NA),
      legend.key        = element_rect(fill = panel, color = NA),
      legend.text       = element_text(color = "#334155")
    )
}

# ---- Inputs ----
months     <- 18
rate       <- 0.015
cost       <- 1200 * 100          # $120,000 per month
p_bonus    <- 0.7
p_win      <- 0.4
bonus      <- 800000
bid        <- 150000

annuity_factor  <- (1 - (1 + rate)^-months) / rate
discount_factor <- (1 + rate)^-months

# ---- Original proposal ----
ev_original <- (160000 - cost) * annuity_factor

# ---- Option A: $152K per month ----
ev_a <- (152000 - cost) * annuity_factor

# ---- Option B: $125K per month + $800K bonus ----
b_monthly  <- (125000 - cost) * annuity_factor
b_bonus_pv <- bonus * discount_factor
b_success  <- b_monthly + b_bonus_pv
b_fail     <- b_monthly
ev_b       <- p_bonus * b_success + (1 - p_bonus) * b_fail

# ---- Option C: RFP, bid $150K per month + gain-share ----
set.seed(15)
n_sims <- 10000

triangle <- function(n, low, mode, high) {
  u  <- runif(n)
  Fc <- (mode - low) / (high - low)
  ifelse(u < Fc,
         low + sqrt(u * (high - low) * (mode - low)),
         high - sqrt((1 - u) * (high - low) * (high - mode)))
}

sim <- tibble(savings = triangle(n_sims, low = 3.2e6, mode = 5.6e6, high = 12.8e6)) %>%
  mutate(share = case_when(
    savings < 4e6 ~ 0,
    savings < 6e6 ~ 0.20 * (savings - 4e6),
    savings < 8e6 ~ 4e5 + 0.40 * (savings - 6e6),
    TRUE          ~ 1.2e6 + 0.60 * (savings - 8e6)
  ))

mean_share   <- mean(sim$share)
median_share <- median(sim$share)
p_zero_share <- mean(sim$share == 0)

c_monthly <- (bid - cost) * annuity_factor
c_win     <- c_monthly + mean_share * discount_factor
ev_c      <- p_win * c_win

# Gain-share tiers (for the decision tree)
tiers <- sim %>%
  mutate(tier = case_when(
    savings < 4e6 ~ "< $4M",
    savings < 6e6 ~ "$4M-6M",
    savings < 8e6 ~ "$6M-8M",
    TRUE          ~ "> $8M"
  )) %>%
  group_by(tier) %>%
  summarise(prob = n() / n_sims,
            payoff = c_monthly + mean(share) * discount_factor)

tier_prob   <- setNames(tiers$prob, tiers$tier)
tier_payoff <- setNames(tiers$payoff, tiers$tier)

# Break-even probabilities (used in the sensitivity analysis)
breakeven_win_vs_a   <- ev_a / c_win
breakeven_win_vs_b   <- ev_b / c_win
breakeven_bonus_vs_a <- (ev_a - b_fail) / b_bonus_pv
breakeven_bonus_vs_c <- (ev_c - b_fail) / b_bonus_pv

# Probabilities at which B or C would be worth at least 10% more than the guaranteed Option A
premium          <- 0.10
win_for_premium   <- (1 + premium) * ev_a / c_win
bonus_for_premium <- ((1 + premium) * ev_a - b_fail) / b_bonus_pv
```

# Summary {scrolling="true"}

## Row

::: {.card}
<div style="border-left: 6px solid #0066FF; background-color: #EEF4FF; border-radius: 6px; padding: 18px 26px; font-size: 1.25rem; color: #0B1F3A; box-sizing: border-box;">
<strong style="color: #0066FF; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em;">My recommendation: Option A, accept the client's offer of $152,000 per month.</strong>
It locks in `r usd(ev_a)` with no risk, while Options B and C add only `r usd(ev_b - ev_a)` and `r usd(ev_c - ev_a)` in expected value in exchange for a real chance of a much worse outcome.
<ul style="margin: 12px 0 0 0; font-size: 1.05rem; color: #334155;">
<li><strong>Lowest risk:</strong> Option A is the only alternative with a guaranteed payoff; Option B has a `r round(100 * (1 - p_bonus))`% chance of falling to `r usd(b_fail)`, and Option C has a `r round(100 * (1 - p_win))`% chance of earning nothing.</li>
<li><strong>Small sacrifice:</strong> choosing A gives up at most `r round(100 * (max(ev_b, ev_c) / ev_a - 1), 1)`% of expected value, and the leads of B and C depend on probability estimates that sit right at their break-even points.</li>
<li><strong>When to reconsider:</strong> B or C would be worth the risk only with stronger odds, such as a bonus probability above `r round(bonus_for_premium, 2)` or an RFP win probability above `r round(win_for_premium, 2)` (see Sensitivity).</li>
</ul>
</div>
:::

## Row

::: {.card title="Summary"}
AstraSync's client rejected a proposed price of $160,000 per month for an 18-month AI/ML implementation that costs AstraSync $120,000 per month to deliver, and offered two alternatives: a flat $152,000 per month (Option A) or $125,000 per month plus an $800,000 success bonus (Option B); if AstraSync declines both, the client will run an RFP (Option C) where AstraSync would bid $150,000 per month plus a gain-share of the client's savings, with a 40% chance of winning. I compared the expected present value of AstraSync's contribution under each option at a 1.5% monthly discount rate, using a decision tree and a `r format(n_sims, big.mark = ",")`-run Monte Carlo simulation of client savings to value the gain-share. The three options are nearly tied on expected value (Option C `r usd(ev_c)`, Option B `r usd(ev_b)`, Option A `r usd(ev_a)`), but they differ sharply in risk: Option B has a `r round(100 * (1 - p_bonus))`% chance of paying only `r usd(b_fail)`, and Option C has a `r round(100 * (1 - p_win))`% chance of paying nothing. **I recommend that AstraSync accept Option A, the most risk-averse choice**, because it guarantees `r usd(ev_a)` while giving up less than `r ceiling(100 * (max(ev_b, ev_c) / ev_a - 1))`% of expected value. Sensitivity analysis shows that B or C would only become worth their risk if AstraSync had stronger odds of earning the bonus or winning the RFP than it currently estimates.
:::

# Analysis

## Row

::: {.card title="Option A (recommended): equal payments of $152,000"}
The client pays $152,000 at the end of each month for 18 months. After the $120,000 monthly cost (1,200 hours at $100), AstraSync keeps **$32,000 per month**.

- PV = $32,000 × `r round(annuity_factor, 4)` (annuity factor) = **`r usd(ev_a)`**
- There is no uncertainty: this is the guaranteed payoff, which makes Option A the **most risk-averse choice**.
- It is `r usd(ev_original - ev_a)` below AstraSync's original proposal (`r usd(ev_original)`), but only `r usd(ev_b - ev_a)` below Option B and `r usd(ev_c - ev_a)` below Option C in expected value.
:::

::: {.card title="Option B: $125,000 per month + $800,000 bonus"}
The monthly contribution falls to **$5,000** (PV `r usd(b_monthly)`), but an $800,000 bonus is paid at the end of month 18 if the implementation beats the client's benchmark (probability `r p_bonus`).

- Bonus PV = $800,000 × `r round(discount_factor, 5)` = `r usd(b_bonus_pv)`
- Bonus earned: `r usd(b_success)` · No bonus: `r usd(b_fail)`
- Expected value = `r p_bonus` × `r usd(b_success)` + `r 1 - p_bonus` × `r usd(b_fail)` = **`r usd(ev_b)`**
:::

::: {.card title="Option C: compete in the RFP"}
AstraSync bids $150,000 per month (a **$30,000** monthly contribution, PV `r usd(c_monthly)`) and earns a gain-share at month 18 based on the client's savings, which follow a triangular distribution (low $3.2M, most likely $5.6M, high $12.8M). AstraSync wins with probability `r p_win`.

- Simulated mean gain-share: `r usd(mean_share)` (median `r usd(median_share)`; `r round(100 * p_zero_share, 1)`% of runs pay $0)
- Payoff if AstraSync wins: `r usd(c_monthly)` + `r usd(mean_share)` × `r round(discount_factor, 5)` = `r usd(c_win)`
- Expected value = `r p_win` × `r usd(c_win)` = **`r usd(ev_c)`**
:::

## Row

```{r}
#| title: "Option C: simulated gain-share of client savings"
ggplot(sim, aes(x = share)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, boundary = 0, fill = "#B7C9E8", color = panel) +
  geom_vline(data = tibble(stat  = c("Mean", "Median"),
                           value = c(mean_share, median_share)),
             aes(xintercept = value, color = stat), linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Mean = accent, Median = warm)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Option C: Simulated share of savings",
    subtitle = paste("Number of simulations:", n_sims),
    x = "Share of savings ($)",
    y = "Count",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme_tech()
```

```{r}
#| title: "Comparison of the three alternatives"
comparison <- tibble(
  Option               = c("A: $152K/month", "B: $125K/month + bonus", "C: RFP at $150K/month"),
  `Expected PV`        = usd(c(ev_a, ev_b, ev_c)),
  `Best case`          = usd(c(ev_a, b_success, max(tier_payoff))),
  `Worst case`         = usd(c(ev_a, b_fail, 0)),
  `Chance of worst case` = c("0% (certain)", paste0(round(100 * (1 - p_bonus)), "%"),
                             paste0(round(100 * (1 - p_win)), "% (lose RFP)")),
  `Gain over A`        = c("-", usd(ev_b - ev_a), usd(ev_c - ev_a))
) %>%
  # Escape $ signs so Quarto doesn't render the cells as math
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ gsub("$", "\\$", .x, fixed = TRUE)))
knitr::kable(comparison)
```

# Illustration

## Row

```{r}
#| title: "Decision tree: PV of AstraSync's contribution (1.5% monthly, 18 months)"
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6.5

# Node positions
nodes <- tribble(
  ~x,  ~y,   ~type,
  0,   6,    "Decision",
  3,   8.2,  "Chance",    # B: bonus?
  3,   3.15, "Chance",    # C: win RFP?
  5.5, 4.7,  "Chance",    # C: savings tier
  8,   10,   "Payoff",    # A
  8,   8.8,  "Payoff",    # B bonus
  8,   7.6,  "Payoff",    # B no bonus
  8,   6.2,  "Payoff",    # C tier 1
  8,   5.2,  "Payoff",    # C tier 2
  8,   4.2,  "Payoff",    # C tier 3
  8,   3.2,  "Payoff",    # C tier 4
  8,   1.6,  "Payoff"     # C lose
)

payoffs <- nodes %>%
  filter(type == "Payoff") %>%
  mutate(value = c(ev_a, b_success, b_fail,
                   tier_payoff["< $4M"], tier_payoff["$4M-6M"],
                   tier_payoff["$6M-8M"], tier_payoff["> $8M"], 0))

# Branches: parent (px, py) to child (cx, cy)
edges <- tribble(
  ~px, ~py,  ~cx, ~cy,  ~label,                                        ~ev,                      ~best,
  0,   6,    3,   8.2,  "b) $125K/month + bonus",                      paste("EV", usd(ev_b)),   FALSE,
  3,   8.2,  8,   8.8,  paste0("Bonus earned (", p_bonus, ")"),        NA,                       FALSE,
  3,   8.2,  8,   7.6,  paste0("No bonus (", 1 - p_bonus, ")"),        NA,                       FALSE,
  3,   3.15, 5.5, 4.7,  paste0("Win RFP (", p_win, ")"),               paste("EV", usd(c_win)),  FALSE,
  3,   3.15, 8,   1.6,  paste0("Lose RFP (", 1 - p_win, ")"),          NA,                       FALSE,
  5.5, 4.7,  8,   6.2,  paste0("< $4M (", round(tier_prob["< $4M"], 3), ")"),   NA,           FALSE,
  5.5, 4.7,  8,   5.2,  paste0("$4M-6M (", round(tier_prob["$4M-6M"], 3), ")"), NA,           FALSE,
  5.5, 4.7,  8,   4.2,  paste0("$6M-8M (", round(tier_prob["$6M-8M"], 3), ")"), NA,           FALSE,
  5.5, 4.7,  8,   3.2,  paste0("> $8M (", round(tier_prob["> $8M"], 3), ")"),   NA,           FALSE,
  0,   6,    3,   3.15, "c) Enter RFP ($150K/mo)",                     paste("EV", usd(ev_c)),   FALSE,
  0,   6,    8,   10,   "a) Accept $152K/month (recommended)",         "Guaranteed, no risk",    TRUE
)

ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = edges, aes(x = px, y = py, xend = px + 0.4, yend = py, color = best),
               linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_segment(data = edges, aes(x = px + 0.4, y = py, xend = px + 0.4, yend = cy, color = best),
               linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_segment(data = edges, aes(x = px + 0.4, y = cy, xend = cx, yend = cy, color = best),
               linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = edges, aes(x = px + 0.5, y = cy + 0.28, label = label),
            hjust = 0, size = 3.6, color = "#0B1F3A") +
  geom_text(data = filter(edges, !is.na(ev)), aes(x = px + 0.5, y = cy - 0.28, label = ev),
            hjust = 0, size = 3.3, color = "#64748B") +
  geom_point(data = nodes, aes(x = x, y = y, shape = type, fill = type),
             size = 6, color = "white") +
  geom_text(data = payoffs, aes(x = x + 0.25, y = y, label = usd(value)),
            hjust = 0, size = 3.8, color = "#0B1F3A") +
  annotate("text", x = -0.2, y = 6, hjust = 1, size = 3.8, fontface = "bold",
           color = accent, label = "Choose A\n(lowest risk)") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#B8C2D0", `TRUE` = accent), guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Decision = 22, Chance = 21, Payoff = 24)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Decision = accent, Chance = warm, Payoff = muted)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1.3, 9.6), ylim = c(1.2, 10.4)) +
  labs(shape = NULL, fill = NULL,
       caption = "Blue branch = recommended, risk-averse choice. Options B and C have slightly higher EVs but risk payoffs of $78K and $0. Gain-share tiers come from the simulation.") +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = panel, color = NA),
        text = element_text(color = "#334155"),
        plot.caption = element_text(color = "#64748B"))
```

# Sensitivity

## Row

```{r}
#| title: "Probability of winning the RFP"
p_win_grid <- seq(0.2, 0.8, by = 0.01)

sens_win <- bind_rows(
  tibble(p = p_win_grid, option = "A: $152K/month",         ev = ev_a),
  tibble(p = p_win_grid, option = "B: $125K/month + bonus", ev = ev_b),
  tibble(p = p_win_grid, option = "C: RFP",                 ev = p_win_grid * c_win)
)

ggplot(sens_win, aes(x = p, y = ev, color = option)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = (1 + premium) * ev_a, linetype = "dotted", color = "#94A3B8") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = p_win, linetype = "dashed", color = "#94A3B8") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(accent, muted, warm)) +
  labs(title = "Expected PV vs. probability of winning the RFP",
       subtitle = "Dashed line = base case (0.4); dotted line = 10% above guaranteed Option A",
       x = "Probability of winning the RFP", y = "Expected PV ($)", color = NULL) +
  theme_tech() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#| title: "Probability of earning the bonus"
p_bonus_grid <- seq(0.5, 1, by = 0.01)

sens_bonus <- bind_rows(
  tibble(p = p_bonus_grid, option = "A: $152K/month",         ev = ev_a),
  tibble(p = p_bonus_grid, option = "B: $125K/month + bonus", ev = b_fail + p_bonus_grid * b_bonus_pv),
  tibble(p = p_bonus_grid, option = "C: RFP",                 ev = ev_c)
)

ggplot(sens_bonus, aes(x = p, y = ev, color = option)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = (1 + premium) * ev_a, linetype = "dotted", color = "#94A3B8") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = p_bonus, linetype = "dashed", color = "#94A3B8") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(accent, muted, warm)) +
  labs(title = "Expected PV vs. probability of earning the bonus",
       subtitle = "Dashed line = base case (0.7); dotted line = 10% above guaranteed Option A",
       x = "Probability of earning the bonus", y = "Expected PV ($)", color = NULL) +
  theme_tech() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Row {height=30%}

::: {.card title="What the sensitivity analysis shows"}
The two most important inputs are the **probability of winning the RFP** and the **probability of earning the bonus**: both are judgment calls, and they decide whether Option B or C is worth giving up Option A's guaranteed `r usd(ev_a)`.

- **Winning the RFP:** at the base case of 0.4, Option C is only `r usd(ev_c - ev_a)` ahead of A, and it falls behind A if the win probability drops below **`r round(breakeven_win_vs_a, 3)`**. But the gain-share has real upside: if AstraSync believed its chance of winning was **`r round(win_for_premium, 2)` or higher**, Option C would be worth at least 10% more than A, and above 0.6 it would be worth about `r usd(0.6 * c_win)`.
- **Earning the bonus:** at the base case of 0.7, Option B is only `r usd(ev_b - ev_a)` ahead of A, and it falls behind A below **`r round(breakeven_bonus_vs_a, 3)`**. If AstraSync were confident of beating the benchmark, with a probability of **`r round(bonus_for_premium, 2)` or higher**, Option B would be worth at least 10% more than A, reaching `r usd(b_success)` at certainty.
- **Takeaway:** at today's estimates, the extra expected value from B or C is too small to justify their risk. Stronger evidence of winning the RFP or hitting the benchmark would change that.
:::

# Conclusion

## Row

::: {.card title="Conclusion"}
I recommend that AstraSync **accept Option A, the client's offer of $152,000 per month**, because it is the most risk-averse choice. It guarantees `r usd(ev_a)` in present value, while Option B (`r usd(ev_b)`) and Option C (`r usd(ev_c)`) add only `r usd(ev_b - ev_a)` and `r usd(ev_c - ev_a)` in expected value. Those small gains come with large downside: Option B has a `r round(100 * (1 - p_bonus))`% chance of paying only `r usd(b_fail)`, its $5,000 monthly margin leaves no room for cost overruns, and the bonus depends on a benchmark the client sets; Option C has a `r round(100 * (1 - p_win))`% chance of paying nothing and would open an existing client to competitors.

The sensitivity analysis shows that the riskier options are not without value. Both leads sit right at their break-even points today, but if AstraSync had stronger evidence of success, with a bonus probability of at least `r round(bonus_for_premium, 2)` or an RFP win probability of at least `r round(win_for_premium, 2)`, Option B or C would offer enough extra value (10% or more above A) to justify the risk.

All three options fall below the original proposal's `r usd(ev_original)`, so AstraSync gives up between `r usd(ev_original - max(ev_a, ev_b, ev_c))` and `r usd(ev_original - min(ev_a, ev_b, ev_c))` in present value whichever it chooses.

**Recommended next steps:**

1. Before accepting, counteroffer between $152,000 and $160,000 per month; every $1,000 per month adds about `r usd(1000 * annuity_factor)` in present value with no added risk.
2. If the client holds at $152,000, accept Option A and secure the relationship.
3. Revisit Option B only if the client agrees to a benchmark AstraSync is confident it can beat, pushing the bonus probability above `r round(bonus_for_premium, 2)`.
:::
